title.suggested: Bill Davis Stabbed While Training for Fight With Tom Allen

summary.suggested: The Missouri Republican reported that Bill Davis was cut on the wrist by a knife-wielding rowdy on Christmas night at Doyle's, near the Fair Grounds, in what it called a plot by Allen's backers before their January 12 championship fight.

metadata.notes: Running head reads 'The Missouri Republican--St. Louis, December 27, 1868'. Before 1888, so not the St. Louis Republic.

facts.fact: A championship fight between Tom Allen and Bill Davis of St. Louis was set for January 12, 1869; the paper called Allen 'of California'
On Christmas night 1868 at Doyle's near the Fair Grounds, Davis's training quarters, rowdies said to be Allen's backers picked a quarrel with Davis and one cut him on the wrist with a carving knife
places: Doyle's, near the Fair Grounds, St. Louis

notes: The article is mostly about the attack on Davis; Allen's backers are only accused by rumor. 'Of California' is how the paper described Allen (302 says Davis is of California and Allen of Cleveland).
